issue_summary.TYPE_CHECK: Technical replicate indices, the right field.
issue_summary.SOURCE_CHECK: The paper describes iTRAQ experiments performed in triplicate and label-free proteomics, but does not explicitly detail the number of technical injections per sample.
issue_summary.TRUTH_CHECK: The mapping assigns a value of 1 to every run. According to the definition, a material measured once gets 1. If multiple runs of the same source are present, they should be indexed 1, 2, 3... unless they are fractions. In this dataset, each source (Sample 1-60) has 4 runs. The paper mentions that iTRAQ-labeled peptides were fractionated into 60 fractions, which were then pooled using a concatenate pooling method. If these runs represent those pooled fractions or different acquisition methods on the same material, they are not technical replicates. However, without explicit evidence of repeated injections of the same material, the default is to check if they are distinct materials (fractions). The paper states "sixty fractions were collected... pooled according to concatenate pooling method... for LC-MS/MS analysis". This implies the runs are likely fractions. If they are fractions, they should all be technical replicate 1.
issue_summary.COMPLETENESS_CHECK: Every run is assigned a value.
